prerequisites: A2 German level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages is recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Know and use a second language to obtain information and communicate ideas within the corresponding professional field.
Integrate into international work groups, and be able to work effectively with colleagues from other languages and cultures.
Acquire transversal knowledge that falls outside the regulated education in this degree but can be useful in any professional field.
Understand instructions in classes and tasks given by a teacher or lecturer.
Understand, with some help, basic instructions and messages (e.g., simple specific texts).
Understand specific vocabulary in the field of mechatronic engineering.
Write simple texts on known or predictable matters.
Express opinions on abstract, cultural, and professional matters.
Present projects related to academic and professional careers in a simple manner.
Function in interpersonal situations in German.
Seek solutions to unforeseen situations using German.
Know the grammatical structures of the German language at an intermediate level.
Communicate in German orally and in writing.

syllabus_topics: Communication in everyday life of general interest. Cultural aspects and courtesy norms in the workplace.
The academic and professional environment (University, company internships, working life).
Projects designed and presented through ICT.
Introduction to the Mechatronics specialty in German.
teaching_methods: Classroom and laboratory practices, language lab (participatory model with communication between students and between students and teachers, oral communication practice, information exchange, individual practice of oral skills, explanation of theoretical concepts and grammatical, lexical, and pragmatic notions)
Group tutorials (for resolving doubts, learning difficulties, exchanging impressions, and individualized complements for level uniformity problems)
Other activities (video viewing, conference attendance, multimedia activities)
Autonomous student work (reading proposed materials, searching or preparing information, writing texts, practical work, preparing activities for classes)

assessment_methods.method: Portfolio (Record and assessment of individual or group work and exercises throughout the course)
Oral presentation of a work guided by the teacher
Written tests (Evaluating knowledge and skills acquired throughout the course: oral and written comprehension exercises, written expression, grammatical exercises)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, assessment is based on a portfolio (20%), an oral presentation (30%), and written tests (50%). For the extraordinary call, evaluation consists of a written final exam (70%) and an oral final exam (30%). If sanitary conditions require it, non-face-to-face teaching activities may be included, and students will be informed of any changes.
